answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
Is this an IT band thing? I cannot tell what this is from a run log, and I will not name a cause. A physio or sports medicine doctor can examine the knee and tell you. Bring the dates, where it sits, and what made it worse: the Thursday hill, the Sunday downhills and the stairs.

Should I still do Wednesday's tempo? No. Wed Aug 19 is swapped for 40 minutes on the bike or in the pool. Quality work comes back only after the knee has stayed calm on several easy runs and a professional has looked at it.

new.analysis:
## What the week shows

The week came to 32.0 miles against 36.0 planned, and nearly all of the gap is the Sunday long run. It was planned at 13 miles easy, but you stopped at 8.5 miles, walked home, and finished at 9 miles. Stopping was the right call.

Everything else went as planned. The Tuesday and Thursday easy runs held about 9:50 a mile at an average heart rate of 138 to 139, the Wednesday tempo ran its middle block near 8:00 a mile, and both rest days were taken.

## The knee is the story

The right knee got worse across the week, and the trend matters more than any one number.

| Date | When it hurt | Pain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Thu Aug 13 | On the hill at the end of the run | 2/10 |
| Sat Aug 15 | Tight before the run, fine during | 1/10 |
| Sun Aug 16 | Sharp on downhills from mile 7 | 4/10 |
| Mon Aug 17 | Aches going down stairs | not scored |

The pain rose on downhill running, which is where the long run went wrong, and it has now reached everyday movement. I cannot tell from a run log what is causing it, and I will not guess. What I can see is a pattern that is worsening, and that is why this week drops the load and removes the hard session.

## Why this plan

Your aerobic fitness is not the limit. Easy pace and heart rate are steady and slightly improving, so the engine is fine and the question is the knee. A full stop would cost some fitness, so the plan keeps short flat easy running only while the knee stays calm, and moves to bike or pool when it does not.

Running volume falls from 32 miles to about 17, and the long run is capped at 6 miles. That keeps you short of the mile where the pain started on Sunday, so the week tests the knee without repeating the same load.

Ten weeks out, a lost week or two of build is recoverable, but a knee that goes wrong in week six is not. The long run goes back toward 2.5 to 3 hours only after the knee has been checked and has stayed calm on several easy runs. The Wexley Lakes goal still stands if the knee settles.
